seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed 3/3 on the answer, and it is in `answer.txt`. I got it by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt` (no interpreter run), and both other seats re-derived it independently.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

The only disagreement was `PRINT CALL outer 1`. The call inside `outer` reads `a` from its own locals, then from the global `a`, which is 0. So it prints 100, not 101. Seat-2 opened on 101, then checked the scope rules and agreed.

I left the room after it concluded.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer and I wrote it to `answer.txt`:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I did not run the program. All three seats traced `program.stamp` by hand against the spec. My first trace put `CALL outer 1` at 101 instead of 100, but scope is per call, not lexical. So `inner` can't see `outer`'s local `a` and reads the global `a` (0), giving 0 + 100. seat-1 and seat-3 had 100, and I corrected mine before proposing.

The vote was unanimous, and I've left the room.

seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 consensus, and `answer.txt` contains the agreed answer. I traced the program by hand against the spec and did not run it in an interpreter. The answer is:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

The only disagreement was the second-to-last value, from `PRINT CALL outer 1`. Seat-2 opened with 101 and changed to 100 after the scope discussion. `inner` has no local `a`, so it reads the global `a`, which is 0, giving 0 + 100 = 100.

I've left the room.
